answer: An agent network can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it can vote on reputation updates. Votes count only after a challenge period, and a randomly selected set of established agents can slash the stake if they show that identities share keys, funding, or coordinated behavior. A cipher can conceal private details while preserving verifiable links; the nebula of pseudonyms still faces the ripple of correlated evidence. To multiply influence, an attacker must lock more capital and risk losing it, not merely mint accounts.
